definitions.explanation: The quality of following a consistent rule, pattern, or order. Used in scientific, mathematical, and general contexts to describe predictable patterns.

examples.japanese: {規則性|きそくせい}が{見|み}られる。
このデータには{何|なん}らかの{規則性|きそくせい}があるようだ。
examples.english: There seems to be some kind of pattern in this data.

examples.japanese: {自然界|しぜんかい}の{現象|げんしょう}には{一定|いってい}の{規則性|きそくせい}があり、それを{法則|ほうそく}として{定式化|ていしきか}したものが{科学|かがく}の{基礎|きそ}となる。
examples.english: Natural phenomena have certain regularities, and the formulation of these as laws forms the basis of science.

notes:
FORMATION: {規則|きそく} (rule, regulation) + {性|せい} (nature, quality). The suffix ～{性|せい} turns a noun into an abstract quality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {規則性|きそくせい}がある: to have regularity/a pattern
- {規則性|きそくせい}を{見|み}つける: to find a pattern
- {規則性|きそくせい}を{持|も}つ: to possess regularity
- {規則性|きそくせい}のない: irregular, without pattern

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {規則性|きそくせい}: regularity, systematic quality (abstract noun)
- パターン: pattern (loanword, commonly used)
- {法則|ほうそく}: law, principle (stronger; a proven rule)
- {周期性|しゅうきせい}: periodicity, cyclical regularity
